title: proto: replace g_assert_not_reached() with REPORT_DISSECTOR_BUG().
description:
Instead of giving a stack trace when the caller passed bad params,
raise a dissector bug, telling what the callee sees. This should
result in a better user experience.

requested review from @JaapKeuter and @AndersBroman

Hi, I added you and Jaap as reviewers since you previously commented on this MR. I'm trying to figure out the best workflow for asking people to review and not lost tracks of merge requests I created or which I'm working on. I ended up to put me as assignee and others as reviewers.

> Do you have a real case hitting this code?

What do you mean? I think it's the opposite: there can't be code hitting the g_ assertions. They're dead code. What I addressed in this MR are

1. more esplicative feedbacks to the caller (dissector bug instead of crash) when the arguments are invalid
1. simpler code where possible: instead of a switch with a single case, I used a IF
1. remove dead code where possible. 2 switches in a row, the first preventing the second, are useless.

Okay, let's review the design rules that are used here:
- Functions exposed on the API for dissectors to use have to check the validity of their parameters, if a (cross-)check fails call REPORT_DISSECTOR_BUG.
- If further on in a function a same check can be done (e.g. in a switch), use a g_assert_not_reached.

The first design rule helps dissector developers to avoid erroneous API use.\
The second design rule is for defensive programming; if the first check is changed somehow, the second check cannot be missed.\
When we start removing code for this second reason, we start shifting reliance from code testing in development to tooling only, something I'm not a fan of.
Ok, then. I will keep the defensive programming part as in the original code, and change the input checks as in this MR.
